FORGEMCP — ANATOMICAL RIG VALIDATION & AUTOMATED DEFORMATION CORRECTION

Milestone ID: FMCP-BLENDER-HAND-ANATOMY-CORRECTION
Status: PROPOSED — NOT STARTED
Depends on: Incorrect finger flexion direction
Prototype: Hand_Rig_Animation_Final_20261030_v002.blend

Objective

Resolve the user-confirmed reverse-bending defect on a recoverable copy of the hand prototype. Establish a labeled hand coordinate frame, verify every joint’s local axis, correct animation signs, and confirm that the saved file moves toward and away from the palm in a way that looks plausible. This is a proposed engineering milestone. The rig was not altered while this proposal was written.

Work packages

  1. Baseline: preserve v002 and its recovery checkpoint; independently reopen the exact input; record Blender and ForgeMCP versions, mesh identity, rig hierarchy, Action, transforms and neutral pose.
  2. Coordinate frame: label palm, dorsal surface, wrist-to-fingertip direction, thumb direction and intended flexion vector from the mesh and the approved neutral view.
  3. Single-joint diagnosis: reset to neutral, pose one joint and one sign at a time, record local matrices and tip paths, and compare all three candidate local axes. Identify roll or parent-space discrepancies.
  4. Direction correction: change only the proven sign/axis assumptions on a new versioned copy. Preserve the existing skeleton and weights unless measured deformation evidence requires a separately reviewed weight edit.
  5. Articulation: produce open, single-digit, thumb-opposition, partial-curl and intended close poses. Avoid forcing a full fist if geometry or contact makes it invalid.
  6. Regression: check isolated finger motion, weight normalization, influence limits, neutral restoration, repeatable Action evaluation, degenerate geometry and likely mesh self-contact.
  7. Visual acceptance: review front, back, side and palm orthographic views. Numerical tests and visual judgments are separate acceptance gates.
  8. Persistence: save a new file, independently reopen it, read back exact objects and Action, and replay the corrected motion.

Acceptance criteria

  • Fingers flex toward the palm and extend back to neutral.
  • Each joint uses the documented anatomical axis and sign.
  • Fingertip paths are continuous and plausible.
  • Adjacent fingers do not move unintentionally beyond measured tolerances.
  • Thumb flexion and opposition are separately intelligible and do not break the web space or palm.
  • Deformation remains stable across the accepted range.
  • Neutral pose restoration succeeds after animation and after save/reopen.
  • A human visual review approves all required orthographic views.
  • Evidence, changed files, remaining defects and exact test boundaries are added to the Encyclopedia.

No ARP, Rigify or custom alternative should silently replace the chosen skeleton. If the existing structure proves unsuitable, record the evidence and propose a separate replacement plan before rebuilding.
